content: Azithromycin ophthalmic solution, commonly known by the brand name Azasite, is a medication specifically used to treat bacterial eye infections. It is not effective against other types of eye infections. Instructions for Use: 1. Preparation: Before using the medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should be done both when starting the medication and with each refill. 2. Hygiene: Wash your hands thoroughly before applying the eye drops. 3. Contact Lenses: Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication or if you have an active bacterial eye infection. 4. First-Time Use: If this is your first time using the medication, hold the dropper upright and remove the cap to release any extra pressure inside the dropper. 5. Before Each Use: Shake the dropper once while holding it upside down, then remove the cap. 6. Application: Tilt your head back and look upward. Gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) with one finger to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye after application. 7. Multiple Eye Medications: If you are using other eye medications (e.g., drops or ointments), wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying the next medication. 8. Consistency: Use this medication regularly at the same time(s) each day to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if symptoms improve earlier. Side Effects: Temporary eye irritation, stinging, burning, or blurred vision may occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to other types of eye infections, including fungal infections. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction. Precautions: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to azithromycin, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin, clarithromycin), ketolide antibiotics (e.g., telithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred. Avoid driving or operating machinery until your vision clears. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if azithromycin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator. Once opened, the bottle can be stored in the refrigerator or at room temperature. However, the medication expires 14 days after opening. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Discard any unused medication after completing the treatment or after 14 days, whichever comes first.
